notes: Step 1 parts are unchanged: Arduino UNO, servo, and three jumper wires (no breadboard, as the circuit image shows the servo wired straight to the UNO).
Connections follow the circuit image and text: servo PWR (red) to 5V, servo GND (black) to GND, servo signal to digital pin 9, which matches myservo.attach(9).

The image shows the black wire going to a GND pin in the power header, next to 5V. The catalogue has GND.1, GND.2 and GND.3 and does not say which is which, so I used GND.2. All the GND pins are the same node on the UNO.
The servo is powered from the UNO's 5V pin, within its 4.8-6 V range. Its signal is 5 V logic from pin 9.
The servo's 3-pin connector is modelled as the servo's PWM, V+ and GND ports, each joined to one jumper wire end.
